meta.title: Nephrology Literature Update
meta.query: Clinical nephrology — RCTs, systematic reviews & meta-analyses (humans, English)
meta.source: PubMed (NLM) abstracts; summaries and appraisals generated automatically from those abstracts. Each entry links to its PubMed record and DOI.
meta.note: Summaries and PICO are machine analyses of the source abstracts; criteria marked “not specified” were not stated. Read the source before acting clinically.
meta.appraisal_source: Automated critical appraisal (clinical bottom-line, relevance, caveat).

articles.authors: Pei X, Gao H, Zhang L
articles.title: Diagnostic and prognostic value of fibroblast growth factor 23 in acute kidney injury: systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 studies evaluating the diagnostic and prognostic utility of FGF23 in acute kidney injury (AKI).

pico.population: Patients at risk for or with AKI
pico.intervention: Circulating intact FGF23 (iFGF23) or C-terminal FGF23 (cFGF23) measurement

inclusion: Studies evaluating circulating iFGF23 or cFGF23 in AKI

appraisal.bottom_line: FGF23 demonstrates moderate-to-high diagnostic accuracy for AKI (SROC AUC 0.87, 95% CI 0.81-0.92) and moderate prognostic value for mortality (SROC AUC 0.77, 95% CI 0.70-0.83). iFGF23 appears more accurate than cFGF23 for diagnosis (AUC 0.91 vs 0.81).
appraisal.relevance: FGF23 could serve as a useful biomarker for early AKI detection and risk stratification, potentially identifying patients at higher risk of death.
appraisal.caveat: Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies (I2 = 67% for diagnosis, up to 86.2% for prognosis), and protocols for measurement are not yet standardized.

articles.authors: Thomas SM, Anilkumar AS, Veerabathiran R
articles.title: Protective association of the ELMO1 rs741301 variant against diabetes mellitus and diabetic nephropathy: a systematic meta-analysis of case-control studies.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 9 case-control studies investigating the association between the ELMO1 rs741301 polymorphism and diabetic nephropathy (DN) in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM).

pico.comparison: Individuals with DM but without DN

inclusion: Studies investigating ELMO1 rs741301 and DN in DM patients

appraisal.bottom_line: The ELMO1 rs741301 polymorphism is significantly associated with reduced susceptibility to DN under allelic (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.67-0.88), recessive (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.61-0.90), and dominant (OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.53-0.88) models.
appraisal.relevance: Identifying genetic protective factors like ELMO1 variants may help in risk stratification and understanding the pathophysiology of diabetic kidney disease.
appraisal.caveat: The analysis is based on a relatively small number of case-control studies (n=9), which are prone to selection bias and cannot establish causality.

articles.authors: Ma J, Liu B, Pang J, Wang P, Li Y et al.
articles.title: Efficacy and safety of ferric citrate tablets in Chinese patients with hyperphosphatemia undergoing maintenance hemodialysis: a multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, phase III trial.
articles.summary: A phase III, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial comparing ferric citrate to sevelamer carbonate for hyperphosphatemia in Chinese maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients.

pico.population: Chinese patients with hyperphosphatemia on maintenance hemodialysis
pico.outcome: Change in serum phosphorus from baseline to week 12

inclusion: Patients with hyperphosphatemia on maintenance hemodialysis

appraisal.bottom_line: Ferric citrate was non-inferior to sevelamer carbonate in reducing serum phosphorus (LS mean difference -0.09 mmol/L, 95% CI -0.24 to 0.05 mmol/L), while also improving hemoglobin and iron parameters.
appraisal.relevance: Ferric citrate provides an effective alternative to sevelamer for phosphate control in HD patients, with the added benefit of treating iron-deficiency anemia.
appraisal.caveat: The trial used an open-label design, which could introduce bias in reporting or management, and the non-inferiority margin was 0.32 mmol/L.

articles.authors: Zhang Q, Gong T, Ye Y
articles.title: The Impact of Educational or Behavioural Interventions on Fatigue in Adults Receiving Haemodialysis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 30 studies evaluating non-pharmacological interventions for fatigue in adults receiving hemodialysis.

pico.intervention: Self-management education, exercise training, or cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)

inclusion: Randomised controlled trials and quasi-experimental studies

appraisal.bottom_line: Self-management education (SMD 0.98, 95% CI 0.69-1.28) and exercise training (SMD 0.82, 95% CI 0.44-1.20) significantly reduced fatigue, while CBT did not show a significant effect (SMD 1.45, 95% CI -0.46 to 3.37).
appraisal.relevance: Fatigue is a major burden in HD; these findings support incorporating self-management and exercise into routine care.
appraisal.caveat: The certainty of evidence was moderate for education but low for exercise and very low for CBT, reflecting potential methodological weaknesses in the primary studies and high variability in effect sizes.

articles.authors: Wang D, Wang Z, Wang D, Lei W, Lu Y et al.
articles.title: Effects of flurbiprofen axetil on postoperative renal function in patients undergoing percutaneous nephrolithotomy: A prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical study.
articles.summary: A prospective, randomized, double-blind trial assessing whether low-dose flurbiprofen axetil reduces AKI in patients undergoing percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL).

pico.population: Patients undergoing PCNL under general anesthesia
pico.outcome: Incidence of AKI and levels of NGAL, cystatin C, and creatinine

inclusion: Patients undergoing PCNL between February and July 2025

appraisal.bottom_line: Flurbiprofen axetil did not significantly reduce the incidence of AKI (1 case vs 5 cases, P=0.207), although it significantly lowered NGAL levels at 6 hours postoperatively (184.84 vs 216.35, P=0.002).
appraisal.relevance: While NGAL (a marker of tubular stress) was lower, the study failed to demonstrate a clinical benefit in preventing AKI defined by creatinine or GFR.
appraisal.caveat: The study was small (n=120) and likely underpowered to detect a significant difference in the clinical endpoint of AKI incidence.

articles.authors: Hsu JW, Wang HP, Chiang TI
articles.title: Role of fibroblast growth factor 23 in predicting CKD progression and prognosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 12 prospective cohort studies (n=21,042) evaluating FGF-23 as a prognostic marker in pre-dialysis CKD.

pico.outcome: Kidney failure, cardiovascular events, and all-cause mortality

appraisal.bottom_line: Elevated FGF-23 is a strong predictor of adverse outcomes, with the highest quartile in advanced CKD carrying a 2.32-fold risk of kidney failure (95% CI 1.80-2.98) and a 1.61-fold risk of all-cause mortality (95% CI 1.40-1.87).
appraisal.relevance: FGF-23 measurement may improve risk stratification in CKD patients beyond traditional markers like eGFR.
appraisal.caveat: The evidence is derived from observational cohort studies, which cannot prove that FGF-23 is a causal factor or a modifiable therapeutic target.

articles.authors: Vidanapathirana M, Wijayaratne D, Ariadurai J, Jayasinghe S
articles.title: Gender disparity in access to care across the continuum of chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.
articles.summary: A systematic review of 35 studies examining gender-based disparities across the CKD care continuum.

pico.outcome: Access to diagnosis, monitoring, dialysis initiation, and transplantation

inclusion: Focus on gender-based disparities in CKD care

appraisal.bottom_line: Women consistently face disadvantages in CKD care, including lower odds of diagnosis, less frequent monitoring, lower rates of AVF use, and reduced access to the transplant waitlist and transplantation.
appraisal.relevance: This highlights systemic inequities that require policy interventions to ensure equitable care for female patients with kidney disease.
appraisal.caveat: The review synthesizes observational data with varying definitions of 'gender' and 'access', and the underlying causes (systemic vs. socioeconomic) were not quantitatively disentangled.

articles.authors: Jia M, Wu Q, Zou J, Jin D
articles.title: A young male with kidney damage from genetic mitochondrial disease: case report and literature review.
articles.summary: A case report and literature review of a 17-year-old male with FSGS and hearing loss due to a mitochondrial MT-TL1 mutation.

pico.population: 17-year-old male with proteinuria, renal dysfunction, and hearing loss
pico.intervention: Mitochondrial energy synthesis support and supportive renal care

inclusion: Case report of m.3243 A > G mutation

appraisal.bottom_line: The m.3243 A > G mutation in the MT-TL1 gene can present as FSGS with hearing loss, mimicking Alport syndrome but requiring different diagnostic and management approaches.
appraisal.relevance: Nephrologists should consider mitochondrial disease in patients with concurrent renal and auditory symptoms, especially when biopsy shows dysmorphic mitochondria.
appraisal.caveat: This is a single case report; the PubMed label 'Systematic Review' is inaccurate as the primary focus is a single patient's clinical course.

articles.authors: Adar A, Kaufman-Shriqui V, Boaz M
articles.title: Nutrition Supplements and Serum Albumin in Hemodialysis: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 8 RCTs (n=382) evaluating the effect of oral nutrition supplements (ONS) or intradialytic parenteral nutrition (IDPN) on serum albumin in HD patients.

appraisal.bottom_line: Nutritional supplementation (ONS/IDPN) significantly increased serum albumin levels (SMD 0.372 g/dL, 95% CI 0.103-0.641, P=0.007) in hemodialysis patients.
appraisal.relevance: ONS and IDPN are effective strategies to improve albumin, a key marker of malnutrition and mortality risk in the HD population.
appraisal.caveat: The total sample size is small (382 patients across 8 trials), and the study uses serum albumin as a surrogate marker for nutritional status rather than hard clinical outcomes like mortality.

articles.authors: Pourrezagholi F, Amini H, Omid Moradi, Mahdavi B, Nadiri Niri A et al.
articles.title: Effect of Melatonin Supplementation on Glycemic and Lipid Profiles in Kidney Transplant Recipients: A Clinical Trial.
articles.summary: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of melatonin supplementation in kidney transplant recipients.

pico.population: Adult kidney transplant recipients (>= 6 months post-transplant)
pico.outcome: Changes in FBS, HbA1c, and lipid profile

appraisal.bottom_line: Melatonin supplementation for 3 months modestly improved HbA1c (beta -0.30%, 95% CI -0.59 to -0.01) and triglycerides (beta -23.77 mg/dL, 95% CI -45.50 to -2.04), but had no significant effect on FBS, blood pressure, or GFR.
appraisal.relevance: Melatonin may be a low-risk adjunct for managing metabolic syndrome in transplant patients, though the clinical significance of these modest changes is unclear.
appraisal.caveat: The study had a small sample size (n=84) and a short duration (3 months), limiting conclusions about long-term metabolic or graft benefits.

articles.authors: Shadravan S, Khezri R, Zarei Venovel M, Mahami-Oskouei M, Hooman N
articles.title: Impact of Dapagliflozin on Kidney Function Decline in Chronic Kidney Disease Patients: A Systematic Review.
articles.summary: A systematic review of dapagliflozin's impact on eGFR decline in CKD patients, excluding secondary analyses of the DAPA-CKD trial.
exclusion: Secondary analyses of the DAPA-CKD parent trial

appraisal.bottom_line: The effect of dapagliflozin on eGFR decline was highly variable across the 4 unique trials identified (MD range -6.60 to +0.93 mL/min/1.73m2), precluding a meta-analysis.
appraisal.relevance: While the landmark DAPA-CKD trial showed benefit, other independent trials show high heterogeneity in eGFR outcomes, suggesting the need for more standardized data.
appraisal.caveat: Extreme heterogeneity (I2 = 93.7%) and the very small number of independent trials (n=4) make it difficult to generalize the effect on eGFR slope outside the DAPA-CKD cohort.

articles.authors: Liu PY, Shih CK, Hsieh MH, Lin CC, Liu CY et al.
articles.title: Cardiovascular outcome of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists vs dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor on end-stage kidney disease patients with heart failure: an emulated target trial in patients with diabetes.
articles.summary: A target trial emulation using EHR data comparing GLP-1RAs to DPP-4is in diabetic ESKD patients with heart failure on dialysis.

pico.population: Diabetic ESKD patients with heart failure on maintenance dialysis
pico.outcome: Composite of ischemic cardiovascular events and heart failure exacerbations

appraisal.bottom_line: GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome (31.7% vs 41.4%; HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.64-0.82) and lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.68) compared to DPP-4is.
appraisal.relevance: This provides rare evidence for the benefit of GLP-1RAs in the dialysis population, a group typically excluded from major cardiovascular outcome trials.
appraisal.caveat: Despite the PubMed label 'Randomized controlled trial', this is an observational target trial emulation using EHR data; while propensity matching was used, residual confounding remains possible.
